title: Branch your database like a cell
label: A round cell labelled main holds four organelles drawn as database tables: users, orders, invoices and products. It buds two identical daughter cells, tagged preview/new-checkout and fix/login, whose tables are dashed outlines because they still share the parent's data. On preview/new-checkout the orders table becomes solid, changes colour and gains a column. The fix/login cell is discarded and dissolves. The changed cell then moves back and its membrane fuses with main, and main's orders table now carries the new column. A log beside it reads branched in 0.8 s, 0 bytes copied.
heading:
Branch the whole
database. Keep
what works.
sub: Every branch is a full copy that costs nothing until you change it. Try the change, throw away the rest, merge it back.
